propositions: The AC1 snapshot equivalence contract in test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py does not actually drive the real MCP and reconciler entry points; instead it re-calls the shared composer with identical arguments, making the cross-surface equality comparison vacuous and unable to catch parity bugs.
The MCP surface block must invoke the real server built via build_server() and call the real explain_criterion tool via asyncio.run(server.call_tool(...)) instead of re-composing the snapshot.

The reconciler surface block must invoke the real rebar_reconciler.__main__.main() argv entry point with --dry-run-enumerate and assert its return code is 0, capturing the snapshot composition that occurs at __main__.py:570.

Both surface blocks must anchor their assertions to absolute expected snapshot content (repo root, envelope version, config keys from project and env provenance layers) in addition to comparing against the Python reference, because cross-surface equality alone remains true if all surfaces are wrong.

The capture mechanism must use module-global rebinding of rebar._operation_config.compose_operation_snapshot at call time to ensure real code paths are instrumented, and must fail explicitly if the recorder never fires, guarding against surfaces that silently stop routing through the composer.
